_comment: Single source of truth for how InChIKey collisions are resolved. Several same-skeleton (block-1) or same-full-key collisions in the catalog are not accidental: some are distinct drugs whose upstream keys were corrupted to collide, some are the same drug split across two rows, and some are legitimate stereoisomer families. This registry unifies the dispositions that used to drift across _DO_NOT_MERGE and _FORCE_MERGE (pipeline/build/sqlite.py) and _KNOWN_INCHIKEY_DUPS (the overlay-integrity test); it is loaded via pipeline/collision_registry.py. The fold families live in isomer-families.json and are referenced here by disposition only. Each cluster is a set of EXACT canonical_name values with a disposition: 'distinct' = different drugs sharing (or having shared, pre-correction) an InChIKey block, which the dedup merge must never fuse; 'merge' = the same drug split across rows, folded into `into`. Corrupt shared keys are fixed separately in IDENTIFIER_CORRECTIONS (Stage 0.0a); this registry records the classification the fixes and guards consume. Stage 0.1 (PSID FAMILY assignment) reads it too.

distinct.note: unrelated drugs; one row carried a wrong shared connectivity block

4-D and beta-D are deuterated mescaline isotopologues (4-trideuteromescaline, beta,beta-dideuteromescaline) — distinct molecules sharing mescaline's skeleton, not a fold. Their names are garbled/truncated (separate cleanup); kept distinct so they never fold their dose data into achiral mescaline

two AMPAkine research dev-codes sharing a skeleton (one flat, one resolved); enantiomer-vs-regioisomer relationship unconfirmed, so distinct by default (never auto-fold an unconfirmed pair) — see isomer-families.json excluded list
plant vs single molecule; Cannabis's structure is nulled in 0.0a so the plant no longer carries THC's key
enantiomers, genuinely distinct drugs (antitussive vs opioid); shared full key corrected in 0.0a (Dextromethorphan -> MKXZASYAUGDDCJ-NJAFHUGGSA-N)

diastereomers; both rows had lost their stereo (identical flat key). Corrected to distinct stereo keys in 0.0a. Default disposition is distinct (see spec open question 3); revisit if a diastereomer fold is ever wanted
4F-PHP had a-PHP's (fluorine-less) structure; corrected in 0.0a to the 4-fluoro key BCJXLSGKMNRRKO
distinct nitazene opioids; Butonitazene had metodesnitazene's methoxy/desnitro structure; corrected in 0.0a to the butoxy-nitro key UZZPOLCDCVWLAZ
distinct tryptamines; 4-HO-DiPT carried 4-HO-MPT's structure/CID; corrected in 0.0a to the diisopropyl key KBRYKXCBGISXQV

merge.note: Marinol is the brand of dronabinol, which IS delta-9-THC; fold the brand row into THC
same drug (3-hydroxy analog of eticyclidone); two rows with identical CID/structure
same drug (N-ethylnorketamine / NENK); two rows with identical CID/structure

same drug; the 4F-PHP row's corrupt (a-PHP) key had hidden this duplicate from structural dedup. 4F-PHP is the standard short name; the richer 4-Fluoro-alpha-PHP row folds into it (data reassigned by _merge_into). Merge runs before the 0.0a key correction, which then fixes the surviving row's key to BCJXLSGKMNRRKO.

One compound under two rows: the theanine in tea is the L enantiomer, and the Theanine row's own key is the L one. The collision was invisible until L-Theanine got identifiers at all (identifier-corrections-manual.json) — it had none, so nothing collided. Keeping L-Theanine: it holds the half-life, the binding row and the Chinese name, and already lists Theanine as an alias. Split, a dose logged as 'theanine' and one logged as 'L-theanine' landed on different substances — two of every graph and every stat.
